newsitem.title: FRANCE: French builders march for state investment.
newsitem.headline: French builders march for state investment.

text.p: Some 6,000 construction and public works bosses marched in Paris on Thursday, calling for state investment to lift the sector out of a slump threatening major job losses.

They were the latest protesters to join a wave of social unrest fuelled by stagnating growth, acute unemployment and state budget austerity. Civil servants and doctors last week staged a 24-hour strike against budget and job cuts.
Sporting hard hats, protesters gathered near the central Arc de Triomphe as cranes unfurled a giant banner reading "Construction, employment, one struggle: stop the destruction".

Alain Sionneau, head of the Construction Federation FNP, said building companies would shed 50,000 jobs in the coming months unless the government agreed to loan local elected bodies 100 billion francs ($20 billion) to invest in construction over the next five years.
FNP says the sector's turnover will slip by two percent this year from last year because of a drop in public investment by the state, regions and municipalities.
France is cutting its budget deficit to comply with requirements to join the single European currency in 1999.
A group of small construction company bosses told reporters after meeting Prime Minister Alain Juppe that he was aware of the seriousness of the crisis.
The government, which a year ago launched plans to grant interest-free loans to help individuals buy homes, says recovery in the building sector has already begun.

Housing Minister Pierre-Andre Perissol said 130,000 people had taken advantage of the loan facility and the number of new dwellings sold during the second quarter of this year had risen by 25 percent over the same period last year.
